**Dentate gyrus.** A 100 × 20 table of weights: part 1's ten columns, plus ten more drawn from a separate Park–Miller sequence (seed + 50,000), each the whole-number part of 4 × s ÷ (2³¹ − 1). A granule cell fires if its total reaches τ.

**Wiring** (one Park–Miller sequence per wiring seed, default 30, drawn in this order):

- mossy fibres: for each granule cell in turn, CA3 cells are drawn until it has 3 different ones;
- perforant path: for each CA3 cell and each input, connected if the draw is below 0.4;
- starting strengths: for each CA3 cell and each input, the draw × 0.3, kept only where connected;
- tie-breakers: for each CA3 cell, the draw × 0.001.

**Storage**, for Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday in that order. For CA3 cell c:

> total = 100 × (active mossy-fibre contacts on c) + Σ over active inputs i wired to c of (strength + learned) + tie-breaker

where learned is 1 if the synapse from i to c was learned on an earlier morning and 0 otherwise. The 10 largest totals fire. Then every recurrent synapse between two cells that fired is set to 1 (both directions, never from a cell to itself), and every perforant-path synapse from an active input to an active cell it is wired to is set to 1.

**Recall.** The same total, with μ in place of 100, gives t = 0. At each update, every cell adds α × (number of active cells it has a recurrent synapse from), and the 10 largest totals fire. Recall stops when the active cells repeat, or after 10 updates. **Without the dentate gyrus**, the mossy-fibre term is 0 at both stages.

**Cues.** Monday's, Tuesday's and Wednesday's inputs; **A third of Wednesday**, Wednesday's active inputs with the first two-thirds switched off (F17–F19); **Garage A only**, the inputs active on both Monday and Tuesday (F1–F8); and **morph step s**, Monday's first s active inputs switched off and their garage-B counterparts switched on.

**Measures.** Overlap counts the cells two patterns share. The cosine is as in part 1. Because every CA3 pattern has 10 active cells, the CA3 cosine is overlap ÷ 10. The averages in step 9 use wiring seeds 1–40 and the state reached when recall stops.

**Every number, and what it does.** Each row changes one number and leaves the rest as in the demo. Values are averages over wirings 1–40 with the garage example. "Shared" is how many cells Monday's and Tuesday's stored patterns share; "third of Wednesday" is how many of Wednesday's cells that cue activates at t = 0; "morph" is CA3's change at morph steps 1 and 5.

| Number | Demo | Where it comes from | Changed to | Shared | Third of Wednesday | Morph 1 / 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| (all as in the demo) | | | | 5.4 of 10 | 9.3 | 0.07 / 0.91 |
| Cells that fire | 10 | Set by hand: sparse, like CA3 | 6 | 3.4 of 6 | 5.4 of 6 | 0.09 / 0.79 |
| | | | 15 | 10 of 15 | 14.0 of 15 | 0.03 / 0.81 |
| Mossy-fibre targets per granule cell | 3 | Set by hand to suit 100 cells; the rat's is about 14 | 2 | 6.5 of 10 | 9.1 | 0.06 / 0.83 |
| | | | 5 | 6.0 of 10 | 8.9 | 0.04 / 0.58 |
| Chance of a perforant-path connection | 0.4 | Set by hand | 0.2 | 5.5 of 10 | 7.6 | 0.05 / 0.77 |
| | | | 0.6 | 5.5 of 10 | 9.7 | 0.05 / 0.89 |
| Largest starting strength | 0.3 | Set by hand, below one learned synapse | 0.1 | 5.4 of 10 | 9.3 | 0.06 / 0.89 |
| | | | 1 | 5.4 of 10 | 8.0 | 0.11 / 0.90 |
| Mossy fibres while storing | 100 | Larger than any perforant-path total | 20 or 1,000 | 5.4 of 10 | 9.3 | 0.07 / 0.91 |
| Recurrent strength α | 1.5 | Slider | 0.5 | 5.4 of 10 | 9.3 | 0.19 / 0.82 |
| | | | 3 | 5.4 of 10 | 9.3 | 0.07 / 0.88 |
| Mossy fibres at recall μ | 4 | Slider | 0 | 5.4 of 10 | 9.3 | 0.19 / 0.91 |
| | | | 20 | 5.4 of 10 | 9.3 | 0.14 / 0.83 |

What the table shows:

- **Robust.** In every row, a third of Wednesday's inputs ends in Wednesday's whole pattern after settling, and without the dentate gyrus Monday and Tuesday share every cell.
- **The mossy-fibre value while storing does not matter**, as long as it is larger than any perforant-path total.
- **Storage overlap is lowest when the mossy fibres reach a little more than 10 cells.** With 2 targets per granule cell (8 contacts on Monday) or 15 cells firing, places are left over, and the perforant path fills them with cells that learned an earlier, similar morning. With 5 targets, the 20 contacted cells tie, and learned synapses again order them towards Monday's cells.
- **Where CA3 jumps depends on the wiring numbers**, so the morph values move. The shape (little change for small steps, then a jump) holds throughout.
- **μ matters at recall.** At μ = 0, Monday's cue recovers 7.8 of Monday's 10 cells on average, and only 4 in the default wiring (step 6).
- **Flipping.** In 42 of 600 recalls with the demo's numbers (40 wirings × 15 cues), the active cells flip between two sets until the 10-update limit (step 7).

## How the CA3 demo was checked {#ca3-checks}

The CA3 model was re-implemented independently in Python, including the random-number generator, and compared with the demo's internal state in a headless browser.

- **Model.** In 16 configurations (each dentate gyrus, wirings 30 and several random ones, and a range of α and μ), the stored patterns, granule-cell outputs, recurrent and perforant-path synapses, every cue's recall at every update, every morph row, the 40-wiring averages with and without recurrent synapses, the lesion panels and the wiring statistics in step 1 all matched exactly.
- **Text.** The generated sentences were checked in every configuration for agreement, impossible counts and claims that do not match the model's state (for example, a cue described as ending in one stored pattern when it ended in a blend).
- **Navigation and layout.** As for part 1: keys, step buttons, `#step-N` addresses, All steps, Reset, the pop-ups and the sliders, at the same eight screen sizes in light and dark themes.

## Files and rendering

**Files.** Keep these together in one folder:

- `dentate_pattern_separation_steps_guide.qmd` (this guide)
- `dentate_pattern_separation_steps.html` (part 1, the dentate gyrus)
- `dg_ca3_steps.html` (part 2, CA3)

The earlier one-page versions, `dentate_pattern_separation_demo.html` and `dg_ca3_demo.html`, are no longer needed. Each demo's only network request is for its typeface (Literata, from Google Fonts); without it, it falls back to Georgia or the system serif.

**Rendering.** With [Quarto](https://quarto.org) installed, run this in that folder:

```bash
quarto render dentate_pattern_separation_steps_guide.qmd
```

This produces `dentate_pattern_separation_steps_guide.html`, a single self-contained page. The `resources` entry in the header copies the demos alongside it, so the buttons keep working. When the guide sits next to the demos, their Why? pop-ups and last pages link back to the matching sections here.

**Opening a step.** Add `#step-N` to either demo's address, with N from 0 to 11 (11 is the closing page).

**Embedding.** Either demo can sit in an iframe; give it enough height for one step:

```html
<iframe src="dentate_pattern_separation_steps.html#step-4"
        title="Pattern separation, step by step"
        style="width:100%; height:720px; border:1px solid #ddd;"></iframe>
```
